name: No direct production mutation
rule: Production infrastructure/application/configuration changes flow through governed deployment/change mechanisms except audited emergency procedures.

name: Immutable artifacts
rule: A deployed artifact is immutable and identified by digest/version; production promotion reuses the same tested artifact rather than rebuilding it.

name: Environment separation
rule: Development, test, staging and production credentials/configuration/state are separated and not silently shared.

name: Production secrets
rule: Production secrets are injected from managed secret systems and never stored in source or release packages.

name: IaC authority
rule: Infrastructure is defined through approved IaC modules/stacks; manual drift is detected and reconciled.

name: IaC state protection
rule: Infrastructure state uses locking, encryption, backups and restricted access.

name: Policy before apply
rule: Infrastructure and deployment changes pass required policy/security checks before production apply.

name: Build reproducibility
rule: Build input/version/toolchain metadata is sufficient to reproduce or verify the release artifact.

name: Artifact provenance
rule: Release artifacts retain build, source revision, SBOM, signature/provenance and test evidence.

name: Promotion not rebuild
rule: Staging-to-production promotion uses the approved candidate artifact and configuration overlays, not a fresh unverified build.

name: Migration safety
rule: Database/data migrations declare compatibility, ordering, validation, rollback/forward-fix strategy and backup/recovery implications.

name: Backward compatibility
rule: Zero/minimal-downtime releases use compatibility windows when application and schema versions overlap.

name: Deployment health gates
rule: Traffic promotion depends on health/SLO/error/functional checks appropriate to deployment strategy.

name: Canary abort
rule: Canary rollout halts or rolls back when configured error/latency/security/business thresholds are breached.

name: Rollback tested
rule: Critical services have tested rollback/recovery procedures; rollback is not assumed possible without evidence.

name: Feature release separation
rule: Deployment and feature activation can be separated through governed feature flags where risk warrants.

name: Observability required
rule: Production services emit structured logs, metrics and traces/correlation sufficient for support and incident diagnosis.

name: No secrets in logs
rule: Logs/traces exclude secrets and protected content unless specifically approved/redacted.

name: SLO ownership
rule: Critical services have owner, SLI, SLO and alert/error-budget policy.

name: Actionable alerts
rule: Alerts map to owner/severity/runbook and avoid unactionable noise by policy.

name: Incident evidence
rule: Incidents preserve timeline, detection, impact, containment, recovery, communications and follow-up actions.

name: Autoscaling bounded
rule: Autoscaling has safe minima/maxima, dependencies and budget/capacity constraints.

name: Retry safety
rule: Retries use bounded attempts/backoff and only apply where operations are safe/idempotent or protected.

name: Timeouts explicit
rule: Network/service calls use explicit timeouts appropriate to dependency behavior.

name: Circuit breaker
rule: Critical remote dependencies can fail fast/degrade safely under repeated failures where applicable.

name: Backup immutability/security
rule: Backups are encrypted, access-controlled, retention-governed and protected from ordinary destructive access.

name: Restore is the proof
rule: Backup success alone is insufficient; critical datasets/services require scheduled restore validation.

name: RTO/RPO evidence
rule: Critical services have approved RTO/RPO targets with recovery design and exercise evidence.

name: DR dependency order
rule: Disaster recovery follows documented dependency/order and validates tenant/security/integrity after recovery.

name: Multi-region caution
rule: Multi-region active/standby or active/active behavior is adopted only with explicit consistency, cost and operational design.

name: Runbook ownership
rule: Every critical production service has a maintained operational runbook and named owner.

name: Maintenance governance
rule: Maintenance windows, expected impact, rollback and customer communications are governed when material.

name: Operational access
rule: Production admin access is least privilege, MFA/JIT where configured, audited and separated from ordinary development access.

name: Patch governance
rule: Runtime/OS/dependency patches follow risk-based cadence, testing and emergency procedures.

name: Cost allocation
rule: Production cloud resources carry governed tags/labels for environment, tenant/shared service, owner and cost center where feasible.

name: Budget alerts
rule: Cloud cost budgets/anomalies alert responsible owners without automatically disabling critical services unless explicit policy allows it.

name: Preview cleanup
rule: Temporary/preview environments expire and clean up resources/secrets/data according to policy.

name: Release evidence
rule: A production release retains exact artifact, configuration, migration, approvals, tests and deployment outcome.

name: Emergency change
rule: Emergency production change remains bounded, authorized, audited and retrospectively reconciled into normal configuration/IaC.

name: Production readiness truth
rule: A component is not labeled production-ready solely because deployment automation exists; required Phase 20/22/28/31 gates must pass.
